Code read: Trusted() checks that each issuer is a CA (IsCa from basicConstraints), every signature, any critical extension it does not know (HasUnknownCritical), and validity for chain[i] only. The anchors are never dated, so 'does not date the trust anchor' holds. keyUsage is listed as known (so a critical keyUsage is not refused) but never read; pathLen and name constraint values are never read (comment at line 288). The step text and claim leave out one thing the check also reads: extendedKeyUsage, which RunForClient uses to require clientAuth. That omission is harmless. All five attack rows of lesson 4 still fail by their named checks.
